HAC Intelligence — The Rojas Report
CMS Healthcare Advisory Committee Member Intelligence
Published: March 28, 2026
============================================================

KEY FINDING: Zero of 18 committee members have any stated interest in expanding physician ownership of hospitals.

============================================================
MEMBER PROFILES
============================================================

--- MEMBER 01 ---
Name: Elizabeth M. Fago
Nickname: The Donor
Title: Founder
Organization: Home Quality Management / Palm Health Partners
Sector: Nursing Homes & Post-Acute Care
Base: North Palm Beach, Florida

Overview:
Nursing home and post-acute care empire operator. Her son Paul Walczak was convicted of diverting $7M+ from employee paychecks to fund personal luxury spending including a $2M yacht. Trump pardoned Walczak in May 2025, weeks after Fago attended a $1 million-per-person fundraiser at Mar-a-Lago. A payroll company co-owned by Walczak and Fago owed $8.3M to the IRS, growing to $10M+ by 2019.

Career Arc:
- Founder, Home Quality Management (Current)
- Operator, Palm Health Partners (Current)
- Managing Member, FW Healthcare Investments LLC
- Advisory Council, Harvard Medical School Systems Biology
- Trump Nominee, National Cancer Advisory Board (2020)
- Board Member, Health Care District of Palm Beach County (Appointed by Gov. Jeb Bush)

Red Flags:
- Pay-to-play pattern: million-dollar Mar-a-Lago fundraiser followed by son's pardon followed by federal advisory committee appointment.
- Nursing home operator on a committee advising Medicaid and Medicare, with direct financial interest in every policy recommendation.
- FW Healthcare Investments sued for $6.3M in 2019 Florida appellate case.
- Trump pardoned multiple nursing home executives convicted of multimillion-dollar fraud.
- No evident policy expertise.

POH Relevance:
Nursing home and post-acute care operator with direct financial dependency on Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement. No stated interest in physician ownership or expanding competitive alternatives to consolidated systems.

--- MEMBER 02 ---
Name: Robert Bessler, MD
Nickname: The Hospitalist Industrialist
Title: CEO
Organization: Honest Health
Sector: Value-Based Care / Hospital Medicine Staffing
Base: Nashville, TN

Overview:
Built Sound Physicians into a $2B+ hospitalist staffing empire across 450+ hospitals in 47 states over 22 years. Named CEO of Honest Health in April 2024, a value-based care company founded by Adam Boehler (former CMMI director, Trump 1.0) and Abe Sutton (current CMMI director). Honest Health raised $140M. Bessler now advises CMS on Medicare policy while his company's founders designed and currently lead the same programs.

Career Arc:
- CEO, Honest Health (April 2024–Present)
- Founder & CEO, Sound Physicians (2001–2023)
- Board of Directors, LifeStance Health (NYSE: LFST)
- Personal investment vehicle, Alpine Glow Capital

Business Interests & Affiliations:
- Sound Physicians — $2B+ revenue, 450+ client hospitals, 47 states.
- Honest Health — $140M raised from NewSpring Healthcare, Welsh Carson, Oak HC/FT, Durable Capital, Rubicon Founders.
- LifeStance Health board — publicly traded behavioral health.
- Invested alongside Towerbrook Capital, Silversmith, Revelstoke, Summit Partners.

Red Flags:
- Honest Health's founders are Trump's CMS Innovation architects — Boehler ran CMMI in Trump 1.0, Sutton runs it now. Bessler is their hand-picked CEO sitting on an advisory committee reporting to the same agency.
- Honest Health's entire business model depends on Medicare risk adjustment and value-based payment, the committee's stated focus area.
- No separation between company financial interests and advisory role.

POH Relevance:
Honest Health's business model is built on Medicare risk adjustment and value-based care contracting. The committee's Medicare Advantage sustainability agenda directly serves his company's revenue model. No stated interest in physician ownership expansion.

Name: David Carmouche, MD
Nickname: The Payer-Provider Shapeshifter
Title: EVP & Chief Clinical Transformation Officer

Sector: Value-Based Care / Managed Care

Overview:
Has personally sat on every side of the healthcare table: insurer, provider, retail disruptor, and technology vendor. Designed payer contracts at BCBS Louisiana, ran provider networks at Ochsner, led retail health at Walmart alongside an Optum/UnitedHealth partnership, and now deploys AI for primary care teams at Lumeris. Every career move traces the consolidation of healthcare by the payer-industrial complex.

Red Flags:
- Sat on every side of the table — insurer, provider, retail disruptor, technology vendor — with expertise in consolidating each.
- Walmart Health partnership with Optum/UnitedHealth was part of UnitedHealth's vertical integration strategy displacing independent physicians.
- Value-based care "enablement" makes MA consolidation profitable. Lumeris profits when large systems, not physicians, control patient attribution.
- Harvard Business School alumnus — understands financial engineering of value-based care from every angle.

POH Relevance:
Every role has served payer-aligned primary care consolidation. Physician-owned practices and hospitals represent the alternative model to everything he has built. No stated interest in physician ownership expansion.

--- MEMBER 04 ---
Name: Clive K. Fields, MD
Nickname: The VillageMD Walgreens Entanglement
Title: Co-Founder & CMO
Organization: VillageMD
Sector: Primary Care Consolidation
Base: Houston, TX

Overview:
Co-founded VillageMD in 2013, which became majority-owned by Walgreens Boots Alliance, then participated in a $8.9B acquisition of Summit Health-CityMD with Cigna/Evernorth taking a minority stake. Walgreens was subsequently acquired by private equity firm Sycamore Partners for $10B+, making VillageMD a standalone PE-owned entity. His committee role gives him influence over the Medicare payment policy that drives VillageMD's value-based contracts.

Career Arc:
- Co-Founder & CMO, VillageMD (2013–Present)
- Physician executive, Accountable Care Coalition of Texas
- Inherited Village Family Practice, Founded 1975, Houston
- Associate Professor, Baylor College of Medicine and UT Houston

Business Interests & Affiliations:
- VillageMD — 680+ locations, 20,000 employees post-Summit acquisition.
- Walgreens majority ownership → $8.9B Summit Health-CityMD acquisition with Cigna/Evernorth minority stake.
- 2025: Sycamore Partners acquires Walgreens, VillageMD becomes standalone PE entity.
- Three-time Modern Healthcare "100 Most Influential." AAFP Physician Executive of the Year 2018.

Red Flags:
- Co-founded what became a $9B acquisition target, now PE-owned. Committee role gives influence over Medicare payment policy driving VillageMD's contracts.
- VillageMD's entire business model is Medicare Advantage risk-based primary care — exactly what the committee is chartered to advise on.
- Cigna/Evernorth minority stake means the nation's second-largest insurer has a financial interest in VillageMD's policy outcomes.

POH Relevance:
VillageMD represents the aggregation of independent primary care practices into corporate platforms under MA value-based contracts — the model that displaces physician-owned independent practice. No stated interest in physician ownership restoration.

--- MEMBER 05 ---
Name: Kyu Rhee, MD
Nickname: The IBM-to-Aetna-to-Community Health Pipeline
Title: President & CEO
Organization: NACHC (National Association of Community Health Centers)
Sector: Insurer-Aligned / Community Health

Overview:
Went from designing coverage policy for 65 million Aetna members to running NACHC — which lobbies the agencies Aetna profits from — while simultaneously sitting on the board of Providence Health Plan, a Medicaid/Medicare participating insurer. Spent a decade as IBM's Chief Health Officer during Watson Health's well-documented failure, which provided "useless and sometimes dangerous recommendations" in oncology and burned $62M at MD Anderson before cancellation.

Career Arc:

- National Health Service Corps community physician

Business Interests & Affiliations:

- Active board seat: Providence Health Plan (Medicaid/Medicare participating insurer, subsidiary of third-largest nonprofit health system).
- CHAI Board (Coalition for Health AI) — founding partners include Microsoft, Google, Oracle, Mayo Clinic.
- Advisory Board, Found (GLP-1/weight loss startup).
- Advisory Board, Grin (dental tech, FDA-listed device).
- World Economic Forum Agenda Contributor. Senior Scholar, Stanford School of Medicine.

Red Flags:
- Active insurance board seat while advising CMS — sits on board of Providence Health Plan (Medicaid/Medicare insurer) while serving on committee that advises on those same programs.
- NACHC lobbies CMS and Congress ($650K–$800K+ annually) while Rhee simultaneously advises the agency being lobbied.
- IBM Watson Health: "useless and sometimes dangerous recommendations" in oncology. MD Anderson project burned $62M before cancellation.
- GLP-1 startup advisory role intersects directly with active CMS coverage debates.
- Modern Healthcare "100 Most Influential" 2025.

POH Relevance:
As former CMO of Aetna (65M members) and current board member of Providence Health Plan, Rhee represents payer-integrated medicine. NACHC is focused on FQHC funding and managed care — not physician ownership. No stated interest in Section 6001 reform.

--- MEMBER 06 ---
Name: Linda Thomas-Hemak, MD
Nickname: The Safety Net Voice
Title: President & CEO
Organization: The Wright Center for Community Health
Sector: Safety Net / FQHCs
Base: Scranton, PA

Overview:
The closest thing to a genuine safety-net representative on this committee. Quintuple board-certified (internal medicine, pediatrics, addiction medicine, obesity medicine, nutrition), Harvard-trained, returned to her hometown of Jermyn, PA to run 13 community health centers. Runs the largest HRSA-funded Teaching Health Center GME Safety Net Consortium in the nation. No corporate ties. No PE backing. No controversies found. One voice among 18.

Career Arc:
- President & CEO, The Wright Center (2012–Present)
- President, The Wright Center (2007–2012)
- Physician, The Wright Center (2001–2007)
- Member, HRSA Council on Graduate Medical Education
- Founding board member, American Association of Teaching Health Centers

Red Flags:
- Institutional funding (HRSA grants, Medicaid reimbursement, 340B) creates modest financial dependency on CMS policy — structural to FQHCs, not a personal conflict.
- One voice among 18 on a committee whose charter prioritizes MA sustainability over FQHC funding.
- NACHC Lifetime Achievement Award 2025 connects her institutionally to Kyu Rhee (NACHC CEO, fellow committee member).

POH Relevance:
Thomas-Hemak represents genuine physician-led community health. Her presence provides the committee credibility it otherwise lacks. However, her institutional interests (FQHC funding, HRSA grants) are distinct from and do not advance physician-owned hospital expansion.

Sources:
1. The Wright Center Bio — https://thewrightcenter.org/leadership/linda-thomas-hemak/

--- MEMBER 07 ---
Name: William J. Gassen, JD
Nickname: The Hospital Lobby's Incoming Chairman
Title: President & CEO
Organization: Sanford Health
Sector: Integrated Hospital System
Base: Sioux Falls, SD

Overview:
Runs a $12.5B integrated health system with 53,000 employees and 425,000 health plan members. The AHA Chair-Elect Designate — will become Chairman of the American Hospital Association in 2027. The AHA spent $29M+ on lobbying in 2023 and is the leading institutional force opposing physician-owned hospitals. The AHA actively opposes H.R. 3022 (Restoring Rights of Physicians to Own Hospitals Act). Gassen also sits on the board of Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR), a technology-driven insurer backed by 8VC.

Career Arc:
- President & CEO, Sanford Health (2020–Present)
- CAO / CHRO / Corporate Counsel, Sanford Health
- Healthcare litigator, Boyce Greenfield Pashby Welk

Business Interests & Affiliations:
- Sanford Health — $12.5B system, 53,000 employees, 2M+ patients, ~425,000 health plan members.
- 2025 mergers: Marshfield Clinic Health System (Wisconsin) and Prairie Lakes Healthcare System.
- AHA Chair-Elect Designate (chairs 2027). AHA spent $29M+ lobbying in 2023.
- Oscar Health Board (NYSE: OSCR) — co-founded with 8VC/Joe Lonsdale backing.
- Chair, Coalition to Strengthen America's Healthcare.
- Four consecutive years Modern Healthcare "100 Most Influential."

Red Flags:
- The AHA is the single most powerful institutional opponent of physician-owned hospitals. Its incoming chairman sits on a CMS advisory committee.
- AHA actively opposes H.R. 3022 (Restoring Rights of Physicians to Own Hospitals Act) — on the record as of July 2025.
- Oscar Health board seat: governs a health insurer while running a $12.5B system with its own 425,000-member health plan — advising CMS on programs both entities profit from.
- Not a physician. JD background — former healthcare litigator.

POH Relevance:
The most significant POH-adverse member on this committee. As incoming AHA chairman, Gassen represents the apex of institutional hospital lobbying against physician ownership. His presence on a CMS advisory committee is a direct channel from the hospital lobby to federal payment policy.

--- MEMBER 08 ---
Name: Dennis Laraway
Nickname: The Cleveland Clinic's Money Man
Title: EVP & CFO
Organization: Cleveland Clinic
Sector: Hospital System Finance

Overview:
Every employer in Laraway's career is a direct competitor to physician-owned hospitals and a direct beneficiary of the Section 6001 ban. He is now CFO of Cleveland Clinic — an $18B system with $934M in 340B drug revenue over three years, $28.85M in federal fraud settlements in the last four years, and Medicare rate advantages of 3–5x over physician-owned facilities for the same procedures.

Career Arc:
- EVP & CFO, Cleveland Clinic — $18B revenue, 23 hospitals (2023–Present)
- EVP & CFO, Banner Health — $12B, 32 hospitals (2017–2023)
- EVP & CFO, Memorial Hermann — $5B+, 19 hospitals (2011–2017)
- CFO, Scott & White Healthcare (~2006–2011)
- VP & CFO, St. Joseph's Hospital / Dignity Health (2002–2006)
- CFO, Seton Health / Ascension (Pre-2002)

Business Interests & Affiliations:
- Cleveland Clinic — $18B revenue, 23 hospitals.
- 340B Revenue: $934M received (April 2020–June 2023) via "rural-referral center" loophole despite being in downtown Cleveland.
- Banner|Aetna — architect of Banner's joint venture with Aetna (CVS Health) to sell insurance in Arizona.
- Federal lobbying: $500,000 + $779,358 PAC contributions in 2024 cycle.
- Faculty at Arizona State and Rice University.

Red Flags:
- $21.25M False Claims Act settlement (2021): Akron General paid physicians above fair market value for referrals — Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law violations. Whistleblower was fired.
- $7.6M settlement (2024): False statements to NIH concealing foreign funding sources on three grants.
- Active class action: deceptive billing practices under Ohio Consumer Sales Practices Act.
- Senate HELP Committee found Cleveland Clinic "did not clearly designate any portion of its 340B savings for patient drug cost reduction."
- No clinical background whatsoever. Finance executive advising on healthcare delivery.
- Cleveland Clinic benefits from the Medicare site-payment disparity: traditional hospitals collect 3–5x more from Medicare than physician-owned facilities for the same procedures.

POH Relevance:
Cleveland Clinic is among the most direct financial beneficiaries of the Section 6001 ban and the Medicare site-payment disparity. Its CFO advising CMS on payment policy is a direct pipeline from America's most prestigious hospital brand to the reimbursement rules protecting its competitive position against physician-owned alternatives.

Sources:
1. Cleveland Clinic Leadership — https://my.clevelandclinic.org/about/overview/leadership/laraway-dennis
2. DOJ Akron General Settlement — https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/regulatory/doj-cleveland-clinic-owned-akron-general-health-system-agrees-to-21-3m-fraud-kickbacks
3. Senate HELP 340B Report — https://www.help.senate.gov/rep/newsroom/press/chair-cassidy-releases-report-on-340b-reform-calls-for-congressional-action

--- MEMBER 09 ---
Name: Dan Liljenquist, JD
Nickname: The Bain Strategist Inside Intermountain
Title: EVP & Chief Strategy Officer
Organization: Intermountain Health
Sector: Hospital System Strategy / Medicare Advantage
Base: Salt Lake City, UT

Overview:
A Bain-trained strategist who wrote Utah's Medicaid growth cap as a state legislator — the first state Medicaid cap in the nation — then became chief strategist for Intermountain Health, one of the nation's largest nonprofit systems. Intermountain owns SelectHealth (a Medicare Advantage insurer, 1M+ members) and Castell ($86.7M in Medicare ACO savings in 2023, second-highest nationally). He advises CMS on Medicare Advantage sustainability while his employer profits directly from MA contracts.

Career Arc:
- EVP & Chief Strategy Officer, Intermountain Health (Current)
- Utah State Senator, R (2009–2011)
- US Senate primary candidate, Utah (2012)
- Management Consultant, Bain & Company Dallas (2001–2003)

Business Interests & Affiliations:
- Intermountain Health — $15B+ nonprofit, 33 hospitals, 385 clinics, 3,800+ physicians.
- SelectHealth — Intermountain's MA insurer, 1M+ members in UT, ID, NV, CO.
- Castell — Intermountain's ACO, $86.7M Medicare savings in 2023, shared $44M with providers.
- Civica Rx — architect and board chair. Nonprofit generic drug company, 80 medications, 1,500+ hospitals.
- Graphite Health — nonprofit health data interoperability platform, board chair.
- UnitedHealthcare ACO partnership for MA members.
- Federal lobbying: $230,000 in 2024. InterMountain PAC: $227,572 in 2024 cycle.

Red Flags:
- The MA conflict is the most material. Advises CMS on "Medicare Advantage sustainability" while Intermountain owns SelectHealth (MA insurer) and Castell ($86.7M in Medicare savings). Every recommendation on MA payment rates directly affects Intermountain revenue.
- Oversaw Intermountain's Government Relations team running the $230K/year federal lobbying operation — then moved to advise the agency being lobbied.
- As Utah state senator, wrote Medicaid cap legislation, then went to work for a system that collects that Medicaid revenue. Classic revolving door, executed with sophistication.
- Dual role: chaired Civica Rx while serving as top strategist for one of its founding member organizations.

POH Relevance:
Intermountain is exactly the type of large nonprofit system whose market dominance was protected by the Section 6001 POH ban. No public statements from Liljenquist on physician-owned hospitals were found. His advisory role on MA policy directly serves Intermountain's SelectHealth MA revenue.

Sources:

Chief strategist of the largest pure-play for-profit behavioral health company in America — 260+ facilities, 70,000+ patients daily — which is under active DOJ criminal investigation, carries a Corporate Integrity Agreement from a prior $17M fraud settlement, and faces $800M+ in fraud settlements and jury verdicts including mass sexual assault lawsuits across multiple states. Business Interests & Affiliations:

- NABH board chair-elect (National Association for Behavioral Healthcare).
- Acadia lobbying: ~$522,500 through Armory Hill Advocates since 2021 on Medicare behavioral health regulations.

Red Flags:
- Active DOJ/SDNY criminal investigation (September 2024) on admissions, length of stay, and billing.
- Grand jury subpoena (W.D. Missouri) same day as DOJ request.
- SEC anticipated document requests disclosed in September 2024 8-K.
- $19.85M DOJ False Claims Act settlement (2024): knowingly billed Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE for medically unnecessary inpatient behavioral services.
- $17M settlement (2019) — largest healthcare fraud settlement in West Virginia history. Active five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement with HHS-OIG.
- $400M and $405M jury verdicts (2023) for sexual abuse of minors at facilities.
- New York Times investigation (September 2024): Acadia detained patients against their will in at least 12 states, holding people until insurance ran out, charging up to $2,200/day.
- $31M in investigation-related costs in Q1 2025 alone.
- Fourth Circuit (February 2025): reversed dismissal of qui tam case alleging fabricated therapy notes and billing for sessions that never happened.

POH Relevance:
Lynch is the chief strategist of a company under active federal criminal investigation with $800M+ in fraud settlements and jury verdicts. He advises CMS on healthcare policy while his company lobbies the same agency. No stated interest in physician ownership.

--- MEMBER 12 ---
Name: Kimberly Brandt, JD
Nickname: The Revolving Door Made Flesh
Title: Deputy Administrator & COO
Organization: CMS
Sector: Government / Lobbying / Private Equity

Overview:
Six turns through the revolving door: HHS-OIG to CMS to Alston & Bird health fraud defense to Senate Finance Committee to CMS Trump 1.0 (led Stark Law reform) to TDY lobbying firm (Pfizer, AbbVie, Elevance as clients, $109.4M lifetime firm lobbying income) to joined board of Noridian Healthcare Solutions (a CMS Medicare Administrative Contractor) in September 2024, then returned to run CMS operations January 2025. She was also accused by House Democrats in March 2026 of providing inaccurate testimony to Congress regarding Medicaid funding deferrals.

Career Arc:
- Deputy Administrator & COO, CMS — Trump 2.0 (January 2025–Present)
- Partner, Tarplin Downs & Young (TDY) lobbying firm
- Board, Noridian Healthcare Solutions — CMS MAC (September 2024–January 2025)
- Advisor, Enhanced Healthcare Partners (PE, 30 portfolio companies)
- Principal Deputy Administrator, CMS — Trump 1.0
- Chief Counsel to Sen. Orrin Hatch, Senate Finance Committee (2011–2017)
- Senior Counsel, Alston & Bird LLP (health fraud defense)
- Director, Medicare Program Integrity, CMS (7 years)
- Special Counsel, HHS-OIG

Red Flags:
- Noridian conflict: joined the board of a CMS Medicare Administrative Contractor in September 2024 and returned to run CMS operations four months later. No public ethics waiver or recusal disclosed.
- Registered lobbyist representing 52 clients in 2023. TDY lifetime firm lobbying income: $109.4M.
- PE advisor turned regulator — Enhanced Healthcare Partners' portfolio depends on Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement she now controls.
- Accused of misleading Congress (March 2026): testified CMS couldn't schedule a Minnesota Medicaid hearing due to "ongoing litigation" — two days later she herself requested the stay. Reps. Pallone and Clarke gave her until April 7 to revise testimony.
- Medicaid deferrals launched against Minnesota, California, New York, Maine, Florida — Democrats allege politically targeted.

POH Relevance:
Led Stark Law reform at CMS during Trump 1.0 — creating value-based exceptions to physician self-referral rules that intersect with Section 6001. Represents the regulatory architecture governing physician ownership. No stated interest in expanding physician-owned hospitals.

- Acting Administrator before Oz — she set the initial direction of the agency in the current administration.

Carlton is the ex officio filter through which all committee recommendations pass at CMS. --- MEMBER 17 ---
Name: Valerie D. Huhn
Nickname: Missouri Mental Health Under DOJ Scrutiny
Title: Director
Organization: Missouri Department of Mental Health
Sector: State Government / Behavioral Health
Base: Jefferson City, MO

Overview:
26-year Missouri state government bureaucrat. No private sector employment, no corporate board seats, no investment interests. Oversees ~7,500 state employees and ~170,000 Missourians served annually. In June 2024 the DOJ found Missouri violated the ADA by unnecessarily institutionalizing 3,289 adults with mental health disabilities under her watch. An active federal class action filed November 2025 alleges 500+ Missourians languishing in jails awaiting court-ordered mental health services, with average waits of 14 months. She now advises the federal committee on "vulnerable populations."

Career Arc:
- Director, Missouri Department of Mental Health (January 2022–Present)
- Deputy Director, Missouri DMH
- Director, Division of Developmental Disabilities
- Budget analyst, Multiple Missouri departments

Red Flags:
- DOJ ADA violation finding (June 2024): Missouri unnecessarily institutionalized 3,289 adults with mental health disabilities. "Almost none" needed nursing facility placement. Missouri's guardianship system functioned as a "pipeline to nursing facilities."
- Federal class action — Darrington v. DMH (November 2025): 500+ Missourians in jails awaiting competency restoration. Average wait: 14 months. Waitlist grew 88% since September 2023.
- $80.7M disability care cuts proposed (February 2026): Huhn acknowledged cuts would create waitlists but did not publicly oppose them.
- No private financial conflicts — the story is institutional failure being rewarded with a federal advisory role.

POH Relevance:
No connection to physician ownership. The relevant concern is that an official whose state has been found by the DOJ to be systematically failing vulnerable populations is now advising CMS on vulnerable population policy.

Sources:
1. DOJ Missouri ADA Findings — https://www.justice.gov/d9/2024-06/2024_missouri_ada_findings_report.pdf
2. MacArthur Justice Center Lawsuit — https://www.macarthurjustice.org/advocates-sue-missouri-department-of-mental-health-for-failing-to-treat-pretrial-detainees-living-with-mental-illness-and-disabilities/
3. Missouri Independent — 500+ in Jails — https://missouriindependent.org/2026/02/05/more-than-500-missourians-await-court-ordered-mental-health-services-languishing-in-jails/
